You need to choose the right building tiles in order to create beautiful residential areas, economic commercials and environmental friendly industries. Building up your city yields money and resources which can be used to build new tiles and to get victory points. Every city requires you to keep an eye on its structure or you will lose points at the end of the game - nobody likes to live next to a nuclear power plant, right? It's nothing more than a monumental task the 1 - 5 architects age 10 and up face in Paul Sottosantis NEOM - Create the City of Tomorrow. After only three generations a new city should rise on their game boards. In order to do so they draft 7 building tiles per generation and add them to their cities. But they have to watch out, because placing the tiles needs planing and strategy. The road network has to be functional, residential and industrial areas shouldn't be placed next to each other and commercials are less efficient if they don't benefit from their surroundings. After about 45 minutes the game ends and one player call themself master architect. Number of players: 1 - 5 Game duration: 18 mn Complexity: 2 / 5 Play Neom and 1414 other games online. Picking Up Tiles 3.3.1 END OF GENERATION: Collecting Income 4 Game End and Scoring 4.1 Tiles 4.2 Neighborhoods 4.3 Goods 4.4 Money 4.5 Pollution 4.6 Ghost Town 4.7 Power 4.8 Final Score 5 Game variant: No disasters [1] 6 Game variant: Random disasters [2] 7 Solo Game 7.1 Scoring Table Game Objective In Neom, you are building a futuristic city over a period of three generations by placing tiles in your city grid. These tiles provide various goods and money that you will need to place other tiles as well as victory points. Every city requires certain structures to be present or it will lose points during scoring. In the end, the player with the most victory points wins. Course of Play The game is played over three Generations (Rounds), preceded by a Preliminary Round , in which you will choose Cornerstone tiles for later use. Each Generation is comprised of seven turns , for a total of 21 turns over the course of the game. In each turn, you will select a tile and take one of three actions with it. After 21 of these turns, you will score your Cities and determine the winner. Playing a Generation The Generations are played in order, beginning with the 1st Generation, followed by the 2nd and then 3rd Generation. At the start of each Generation, take the corresponding Generation tiles and deal each player a hand of 8 tiles . With this hand, play 7 turns as follows: A. Select a Tile B. Take an Action C. Pick Up Tiles The Generation ends after the 7th turn, in which you have a choice of 2 tiles in your hand. Then you receive income from the tiles in your City, before the next Generation is played in the same fashion. After receiving income at the end of the 3rd Generation, the game ends and scores are tallied. A. Selecting a Tile All players now simultaneously evaluate their hands of tiles, without showing them to the other players. Select one tile. The other Tiles are passed to the left player at the end of turn. B. Taking an Action Normally, you can take one of the following three actions: - Place the Selected Tile - Place a Cornerstone Tile - Sell the Tile for Money ACTION: Placing the Selected Tile To place the selected Generation tile, you must meet the requirements shown in the top left corner of the tile. If no requirement is shown, you can place the tile right away. If you cannot meet the requirement, you must choose a different action. [Rating: 2/10] A drafting game with serious 7 Wonders vibe, which itself feels problematic: in the sort of gaming groups that exist nowadays, where games are played a handful of times at most, the demands of a drafting game are just too much and invariably it is the case of one or more players conducting either insufficient or too much hate drafting, 'throwing' the result to another player - it almost feels random who ends up as the victor.  I suspect that is even more the case here than in 7 Wonders, as NEOM is essentially adding even more complexity (not too much to be make it difficult to understand, but 

[Rating: 2/10] Basically a tile version of 7 Wonders mixed with a board game version of the computer game Sim City.  Drafting tiles instead of cards, and placing them on your board to build a city with various scoring paths.

[Rating: 3/10] NEOM is drafting tableau builder where players have a small spatial puzzle while building a city. Comparisons to 7 Wonders are well deserved. This is 7 wonders, with little difference. When it comes to the tile placement, it is visually reminiscent to Quadropolis, but cannot compare to its puzzle. As for drafting, it is so similar to 7 Wonders, all the pros and cons of that game are here. If there was a way to have such a wide variety of tiles but not bog down layers with iconography, there would be something special in NEOM. As it stands, NEOM is a well designed game that happily mimics other

Wenn derjenige, der rechts sitzt, ähnliche Siegpunktkarten rauszieht wie ich, habe ich das Spiel schon verloren, da er ja auch beim Draften vor mir dran ist und alles passende rausziehen kann (Draftrichtung wechselt nie!!!). [Rating: 3/10] Nothing you haven't seen before but not unpleasant. The disasters were the worst part.

[Rating: 3/10] Basically just 7-wonders the tile-laying game. But nothing too interesting with the tile-laying... just more of the same points for adjacency, route connecting mechanisms I’ve gotten bored of.

[Rating: 3/10] Oh my. What a mess. Drafting, placing, building up a bizarrely complex, yet unexciting scoring system. Doesn't take forever, but boredom is guaranteed. I don't like the artwork either, even without taking the small icons into account. If you don't like 7 Wonders, run for cover.

[Rating: 4/10] A combination of 7 Wonders + Leaders expansion closed-drafting and tile laying. I'm not as keen on closed drafts these days, and the tile-laying, while serviceable, isn't particularly gripping.  I heavily disagree with the notion of many online that the disaster tiles are a bad thing or to be taken out.

[Rating: 4/10] The box design and name are the only unique aspects of this game. The game is just a standard tile draft, the tile design is poor, and many of the symbols are unintuitive. I'd rather play 7 Wonders or Between 2 Castles, neither of which I really enjoy!
